name: effects-smil-animated-bug
exporter: Figma - Export > SVG, then hand-edited in VS Code to add SMIL animation
story: A student exported a corner bug from Figma and then followed a "animate SVG without JavaScript" tutorial, adding a pulsing dot, a drifting group and a delayed colour flip - all of it SMIL.
idioms: <animateTransform attributeName="transform" type="translate" values="…" dur="6s" repeatCount="indefinite"> as the FIRST child of a named group, before any shape
two <animate> elements nested inside the <circle> they animate, one on r and one on opacity
<set attributeName="fill" to="#F6A623" begin="4s"/> inside the <rect> it recolours - the SMIL element that is not named "animate" anything
the tutorial's own habits (values lists with semicolons, repeatCount="indefinite", bare second durations) sitting inside otherwise untouched Figma output

the Figma shell around it: no XML declaration, zero indentation, fill="none" on the root, uppercase hex, fill="white" as a keyword, xml:space="preserve" plus style="white-space: pre" on text, letter-spacing in em, one positioned tspan per line with a fractional baseline
whyThisMatters: Rule 5 of docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md and §8 both promise SMIL is removed and the removal is reported, and nothing in the corpus had ever carried a single SMIL element - the promise was pinned by no file at all. The removal is also the one sanitizer case that deletes elements from INSIDE the artwork rather than from around it: the <animate> children sit within a <circle> and a <rect> that must stay, the <animateTransform> is the first child of the group holding everything, and <set> is easy to forget because its name does not contain "animate". A shape or a text layer taken down with the motion would be a silent loss of the design.
